name: VeriChain
tagline: A platform where autonomous AI agents run, act and transact, with every consequential action recorded in a log anyone can verify.

audience.concern: Record what an agent is authorized to do and does, without building the accountability layer yourself.
Run agents under policy, with audit-ready evidence, approvals and a kill switch.
Verify what an agent did from an evidence pack, offline, against the minimum assurance you set.
Check an agent's authority and history without having to trust its operator.

highlights.title: Evidence you can check offline
highlights.text: Actions are written to a witnessed, append-only log. Inclusion and consistency can be verified without contacting the operator.

highlights.title: Intent is recorded before effect
highlights.text: A hosted agent’s intent is written down before any action takes place, so a missing record is itself visible.

highlights.title: Honest assurance levels
highlights.text: Every record states its assurance (A0 to A3) and completeness (C0 to C3), and the verifier enforces the minimum you require.

highlights.title: Runs small, scales out
highlights.text: Deployment topologies run from a single machine for development (T0) to federated operation (T3).

verifyIt: Build a demo evidence pack, verify it with vcv, then use the tamper buttons in the dashboard or edit one byte and verify again: the checks turn red.

demo.title: Verify an evidence pack
demo.summary: Check a signed evidence pack, then tamper with it and watch the checks fail. The in-browser verifier is planned; this page shows a labeled placeholder until it ships.

status: Pre-release: specification frozen, core log and verifier built

buildFromSource.title: Build from source
buildFromSource.intro: VeriChain is pre-release and has no packaged binaries. Build the log daemon and the verifier from source.
buildFromSource.steps:
git clone https://github.com/intellica-ai-llc/verichain
cd verichain
cargo build --release -p vcd -p vc-verify
./target/release/vcv version

faq.q: Is VeriChain available to use today?
faq.a: It is pre-release. The specification is frozen and the core log and verifier crates are built and tested. You can build it and run the local demo; there is no hosted service or packaged download yet.

faq.q: What does a failed check mean?
faq.a: The verifier reports which check failed (for example the signature, an inclusion proof or the witness quorum). Exit code 1 means a check failed; the JSON report names it.

faq.q: Why does the verifier need my own trust file?
faq.a: A pack carries its own trust anchors, which say nothing about who you trust. Without your trust and policy files the report only shows the pack is consistent with itself.

faq.q: Can I run a pilot server on free hosting?
faq.a: The repository has a pilot runbook for Oracle Cloud Always Free with HTTPS, backups and monitoring. It is for testing only, with no SLA.
